finding: On an average day, 36 of Chicago’s 124 ‘L’ stations sit in transport noise of 65 dB or more. At 19, all in expressway medians, the road is the loudest source. The loudest of all are on the Orange Line, built along freight railroad lines.

ledger.source: Bureau of Transportation Statistics, National Transportation Noise Map (2022 release)
ledger.units: 124 city ‘L’ stations, 9,844 CTA bus stops, 2,746,388 residents (2020 Census)
method: Modelled road (2023 traffic), rail (2022, incl. the ‘L’ and freight) and aviation (2022) noise, LAeq,24h on 30 m cells, combined by energy
Each point reads the median within 90 m; a station reads its loudest platform (CTA GTFS 8 Nov 2026)
Map: one dot per block, the energy average of that surface over the block
Midway check: CDA aircraft-noise monitors, 12 months to December 2025
caveats: A model, not a measurement: buildings and barriers do not block sound in it, so dense streets read louder than they are
Nothing below 45 dB is mapped; local streets without traffic counts are absent
Outdoors only: subway platforms read quiet although tunnels are the loudest ride inside the train
